title: Existence bound via union bound
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite nonempty field, let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $k \ge 1$, and let $d$ be a positive integer. Regard an $n \times k$ matrix $G$ over $\alpha$ as a map sending a message $x \in \alpha^{k}$ to the length-$n$ codeword $Gx$. Then the number of such matrices $G$ for which some nonzero message $x$ has $\mathrm{wt}(Gx) < d$ is at most
\[
(\abs{\alpha}^{k} - 1)\cdot \abs{\alpha}^{\,nk - n}\cdot \abs{B_{d-1}(\mathbf 0)},
\]
where $\mathrm{wt}$ denotes Hamming weight and $B_{d-1}(\mathbf 0)$ is the Hamming ball of radius $d-1$ about the all-zero codeword of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: alphabet α is a finite nonempty field
G ranges over n×k matrices over α
counts G admitting a nonzero message x
with weight of the codeword Gx less than d
